citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
On Aug. 6, 2026, an adult Rhesus Macaque underwent a second major operative procedure due to a clerical and/or
identification error. The macaque was appropriately assigned to the IACUC approved protocol that has scientific and
veterinary reasons for additional major operative procedures but was mis-identified as the animal needing additional
surgery. The animal recovered from the surgery with no lasting welfare concerns based on veterinary assessment.
Animals that undergo major operative procedures and are recovered are subjected to stress, pain, and discomfort.
No animal will be used in more than one major operative procedure from which it is allowed to recover, unless: justified for
scientific reasons; required as routine veterinary procedure; or as determined by the Administrator on an individual basis.
The facility identified this incident and reported it to the overseeing IACUC and took corrective measures.
Correction: ensure correction measures are maintained from this date (Oct. 30, 2026) forward.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
